title: Building a Reliable Testing Strategy
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its role in reliable software.
Identify the topic in code or a realistic scenario.
Trace behavior and describe the expected result.
Apply the concept and verify it using a suitable test.

understand.concept: A testing strategy combines test levels, coverage priorities, risk, automation, test data, environments, and feedback speed. A balanced approach uses fast focused checks frequently, broader integration and system tests at suitable points, and exploratory or manual testing where automation is unsuitable. Testing is continuous and should reflect the product's risk.
understand.whyItMatters: No single test type catches every defect. A layered strategy balances confidence, speed, cost, and maintainability while focusing effort on the most consequential failure modes.
understand.analogy: A careful process uses defined expectations, evidence, and repeatable checks to reduce uncertainty.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies software quality; the actual techniques depend on project context, tools, architecture, and risk.

explain.narrative: Map important user workflows and risks. Choose test levels for each behavior, identify test data and environment needs, automate repeatable checks, plan exploratory checks, define what passing means, and decide how failures block or inform releases. Revisit the strategy as the system changes.

commonMistakes: Prioritizing test count instead of risk and meaningful coverage.
Using unrealistic test data or environments.
Ignoring flaky tests and slow feedback loops.
